comparator.name: Human Resource Studies (Personeelwetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: 2025–26 detailed public curriculum with 2026–27 OER confirmation, checked 2026-10-06
comparator.sourceNotes: The detailed official programme page available on the check date still labels its curriculum 2025–26, while Tilburg’s official OER portal lists the programme in the current 2026–27 regulations. The published detailed structure accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in each of years 1 and 2, then a 30-ECTS open mobility window, one 6-ECTS constrained professionalisation elective, two further 6-ECTS courses and a 12-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded. The discrepancy is preserved rather than silently relabeling the detailed table.
components: Vrije keuzeruimte: exchange, stage of minor
Genuine 30-ECTS mobility, internship or minor space; no elective content is invented.
One of two constrained 6-ECTS professionalisation electives is instantiated neutrally.

routeSelection.basis: The official detailed curriculum requires one of two 6-ECTS professionalisation electives without identifying either as the general route. Coaching en Ontwikkeling is listed first and is therefore instantiated as a neutral official-order tie-break; the choice was made before and independently of UCR course selection.

core: Human-resource management, strategic personnel policy and the relationship between organisational performance and employee well-being
Psychological and sociological analysis of people, work, organisations and organisational behaviour
Employee well-being, workplace health, stress, development, coaching and assessment
People analytics and evidence-based human-resource research and decisions
Labour relations, employment law and the future of work
adjacent: Teamwork, social capital and employee development in organisational settings
questions: How can organisations balance performance with employee health, development and well-being?
How can research and people analytics support evidence-based personnel decisions?
How do law, technology and changing labour relations reshape the future of employment?

candidates.label: Workplace psychology, well-being and employee development
Labour relations, institutions and the future of work

selection.assessment: The closest programme owns strategic HRM, people analytics, evidence-based decisions, financial consequences, teamwork and the general people-work-organisation relationship. Workplace psychology, health, well-being and development form a coherent second route, while labour relations, employment law and the future of work form a distinct institutional route. Both exceed the 30-ECTS distinctness floor. Three alternatives is the maximum, and every generator-eligible interest has one construction owner.

alternatives.label: People, organisations & strategic HRM
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines organisational behaviour, leadership, sociology, psychology, economics, strategy, communication and research around managing people at work.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Human Resource Studies: an interdisciplinary programme on people, work and organisations combining strategic management, organisational psychology, sociology, economics, communication and evidence-based research.
progression: Foundations in economics, politics, law, sociology, psychology, organisations and research precede advanced organisational psychology, leadership, negotiation, public economics, social theory, international business and applied inquiry. Existing validated schedules respect prerequisites and planned offerings; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Workplace psychology, well-being & development
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres psychological science, health, development and assessment while retaining organisational leadership, sociology, communication and research.
alternatives.concept: A workplace-psychology direction focused on employee health, stress, well-being, development, assessment and social behaviour, supported by organisational leadership, sociology, communication and empirical methods.
progression: Behavioural, biological, social, organisational and research foundations precede statistics, cognition, lifespan development, health, abnormal psychology, psychodiagnostics and advanced organisational leadership. The component schedules are reused from validated UCR pathways and retain prerequisite order and planned availability; eleven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, fourteen courses shift the centre of gravity from strategy, business, economics, law and organisational communication to behavioural science, health, development, assessment and psychological research. The difference exceeds the 30-ECTS floor.

alternatives.label: Labour relations, institutions & people policy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum gives sustained weight to employment institutions, law, European governance, political economy, sociology and the policy environment of work.
alternatives.concept: An institutional people-policy direction examining labour relations and the future of employment through law, politics, European governance, economics, sociology, organisational research and international business.
progression: Introductory politics, history, sociology, economics, law and research precede constitutional, European and international law, political economy, advanced institutions, social theory and independent inquiry. The schedule is reused from a validated UCR pathway and respects prerequisites and offerings; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, thirteen courses replace leadership, psychology and organisational communication with constitutional and international law, European history, political institutions, social movements and transnational governance; it also differs from the workplace-psychology route by eighteen courses.

notes.text: Tilburg prescribes a dedicated HRM sequence with labour law, work-and-health psychology, people analytics, consulting, a professionalisation elective and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can construct coherent interdisciplinary routes in people and organisations, workplace psychology and labour institutions, but it does not reproduce the complete specialist HRM or methods sequence; the 30-ECTS open mobility space remains unfilled.
The Tilburg programme is Dutch-taught, whereas UCR is English-taught. This comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language of instruction.

On 6 October 2026 Tilburg’s detailed public curriculum table was still labelled 2025–26, while the official OER portal listed current 2026–27 regulations for B Personeelwetenschappen. The comparison preserves that discrepancy and does not claim the detailed table itself is labelled 2026–27.
